list: The official 55 trophies. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guides are original to this entry and built only from those official descriptions; where a description names no location, count or step, the guide says so plainly.
note: Grand Theft Auto VI is unreleased, so no guide here can rest on played experience. Every guide below is grounded in the trophy's official description plus the Exophase / PSNProfiles trophy list, and it flags every detail the official description does not state.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Work through the roadmap in this guide — story first, then the missable moments before any point of no return, then the stranger strands, collectibles and activity grinds — and finish with 100% completion, which is itself a gold trophy. Because the game is unreleased, the exact unlock order of the last few trophies cannot be confirmed from the official description alone; the roadmap orders them by what each description asks for. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description
Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to the end of its final objective and the trophy unlocks when the mission completes. It is the first story trophy, so it should come naturally on any playthrough. Treat it as missable only in the cautious sense: the official description does not say whether missions can be replayed, so finish the mission cleanly rather than assuming a replay. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. Chapters are completed in order, so this is the first chapter trophy and cannot be earned out of sequence. The official description does not name the chapter's missions or its length, so follow the in-game mission flow and do not skip story content. trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own completion checklist. This is the second gold trophy and the last one most players earn before the platinum. The official description does not list what counts toward 100% — story missions, stranger strands, collectibles and activities are the usual ingredients, and this guide's roadmap covers all of them — so track the in-game completion percentage as you go and mop up whichever category it shows as unfinished. Leave this to the end of the roadmap. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts in total. A stunt is a driving or riding feat the game counts — jumps, near misses and similar moments — and the counter is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so ordinary driving adds to it. The official description does not define which moves count as a stunt or name a best location, so do not grind it early: let the total build naturally through the story and side content, then top it up with repeated jumps in free roam if the counter is short. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. The trophy list records 9 activity types, and one attempt at each is enough — you do not need to win or complete any of them. The official description does not name the 9 types, so use the activities this list itself names as a checklist — shooting range, drone racing, racing, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and the stranger strands — and try each kind the game offers as it unlocks. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Every challenge must be golded — a silver or bronze on even one of them leaves the trophy locked. The official description does not name the ranges' locations or the weapon each challenge uses, so visit the shooting range when it unlocks, work through the challenges weapon by weapon, and use the range's own medal display to find the ones still below gold. This is one of the longer skill grinds, so expect to return to it after the story. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every one of the 14 locations. Each location needs its own win, so a win at one place does not cover another. The official description does not name the 14 locations or where each race starts, so open the race at each location you find, win it, and check the race menu for the locations still unwon. trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different matters: winning the same race 20 times does not count, so you need victories across 20 distinct race events. The official description does not name the races or their locations, so enter every race type the game offers — street races and any others that appear — and keep a note of which ones you have already won. The character-strand trophies in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of the strands; the description does not name the other three, so explore the map for stranger markers and keep a count of finished strands. trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges in total. Challenges are the game's assorted side objectives, and the counter is cumulative, so any 50 across any types count. The official description does not list the challenges or say which are easiest, so open the challenges menu early, pick off the ones that overlap with what you are already doing — driving, shooting, exploring — and let the total build through the playthrough. trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star Wanted Level and then lose it and escape. Both parts matter: the wanted level must reach 4 stars while your partner is with you, and you must then break line of sight and stay hidden until it clears. The official description does not say how to reach 4 stars quickly or where to hide, so do it during a story stretch where your partner is present — the description ties the trophy to having your partner along, and the game is unreleased, so do not assume a free-roam partner is available at any time. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops one after another without losing your Wanted Level — the wanted level must stay active across all three robberies. If it drops to zero between shops, the chain breaks and you start again. The official description does not name which shops count or how close together they must be, so pick three shops near each other, move fast between them, and keep your partner with you throughout. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle counts when the game registers it as newly discovered, so driving the same car model again adds nothing. The official description does not say how discovery is registered or whether it needs entering the vehicle, so get into — or at least approach — every new vehicle type you see, and vary the cars, bikes, boats and aircraft you use as you travel. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. All five must fall before that one use ends — five across two uses does not count. The official description does not say how long Combat Focus lasts or how it is charged, so set it up deliberately: find a spot with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus with them in range, and take them down quickly before it runs out. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport: take an aircraft and leave the airport without a scheduled flight. The official description does not say which aircraft counts or which runway to use, so get into a plane at VCIA and take off on your own terms. It is a free-roam stunt trophy, so it can be attempted any time you can reach the airport and an aircraft. Sources: the official PlayStation trophy description; the Exophase / PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at any point. The whole robbery must stay undetected — being spotted, even briefly, fails it and means starting over. The official description does not name a jewelry store or say what counts as detected, so pick a quiet moment, move carefully, and if the alarm goes up, abandon the attempt and try again rather than fighting through. trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault counts only if you get away clean afterwards, so five robberies without escapes earn nothing. The official description does not name the banks or say how a vault robbery starts, so attempt vaults one at a time, plan the getaway before going in, and escape fully before starting the next. The official description does not say where armored trucks travel or how to stop one, so watch for one on the road, stop it, take its cargo, and break away before the police close in. trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. The counter is cumulative across every shop, so ordinary purchases — weapons, clothes, vehicles, supplies — all add up. The official description does not say which shops count, so just buy what you need through the playthrough and the total will build; if it falls short late on, spend the remainder on anything useful. trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Each garage must be bought, so the trophy is a money and exploration task: earn enough and find all eight. The official description does not name the garages or their prices, so buy each garage property as you find it and check the property menu for the ones still unbought. trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Each vehicle must be registered through the app, so ten separate registrations are needed. The official description does not say which vehicles can be registered or how registration works, so open the Scooter Bros app with a vehicle and register it, then repeat with nine more different vehicles.
